criterion: Study status is labelled and claims stay inside it
guiding_question: Does the paper state whether it reports a plan or completed empirical work, and do its claims stay inside that status?
score_0_anchor: Status is not stated, or planned or untested work is presented as a completed result or as validated.
score_1_anchor: Status is stated, but at least one claim goes beyond it (for example a future method described as shown).
score_2_anchor: Status is stated in the title or abstract; every result claim is backed by reported work; and planned work is labelled as planned.
source_location: PLAN: Title; Abstract. CASE: Title; Abstract

criterion: Model-performance reporting is specified for comparison
guiding_question: Are model-performance outcomes named and specified (or, for a plan, specified for later reporting) in a form another study could use for model comparison?
score_0_anchor: No model-performance metric, unit, or report format is named.
score_1_anchor: A metric or report need is named, but the definition, unit, scale, or per-condition values (or planned format) are missing.
score_2_anchor: Every named model-performance metric has a definition and unit or scale, and values or a planned comparable report format are given.

criterion: Quality-task process is defined for each named phase
guiding_question: If the paper proposes or applies a QA or quality process, does it define the quality task at each named phase? NA allowed if no QA or quality process is proposed or applied.
score_0_anchor: Phases or quality tasks are not defined, or are named only as goals.
score_1_anchor: At least one phase or process part is named, but the task, timing, role, or output is missing for a named part.
score_2_anchor: Every named phase or process part states its task, timing or trigger, responsible role, and output.

criterion: Evaluation or validation method names who is involved
guiding_question: Is an evaluation or validation method named, and is the participant or sample group stated?
score_0_anchor: No evaluation or validation method is named.
score_1_anchor: A method is named, but the procedure or the participant count or selection is missing.
score_2_anchor: The method, procedure, and participant or sample group (role and count or selection) are all stated.

criterion: Feasibility and acceptance are separate questions
guiding_question: When a method or process is evaluated, are feasibility and acceptance posed as separate questions with separate evidence? NA allowed if the paper does not evaluate a method or process intended for adoption.
score_0_anchor: Neither question is assessed, or both are merged into one works-well judgment.
score_1_anchor: One of the two is assessed separately, or both are named but share undifferentiated evidence.
score_2_anchor: Both are posed as distinct questions, and each has its own evidence and conclusion.

guiding_question: If desk-checking or an author self-review is discussed, is it defined as a checklist-guided self-review rather than a structured inspection? NA allowed if the paper does not discuss desk-checking or a review process.
score_0_anchor: A review process is discussed but not defined, or it is defined as a structured inspection.
score_1_anchor: The process is called desk-checking or self-review, but the checklist or the before-check-in timing is missing.
score_2_anchor: The text defines desk-checking as a checklist-guided self-review before check-in and states that it is not a structured inspection.

criterion: Important variants or configurations are covered or excluded
guiding_question: Does the paper state which variants or configurations its results cover, and that at least one important variant is not covered? NA allowed if the paper claims no results and names no variants or configurations.
score_0_anchor: No statement of covered or excluded variants or configurations.
score_1_anchor: A coverage limit is named at a general level, but covered variants are not enumerated.
score_2_anchor: Covered variants or configurations are enumerated, and at least one important uncovered variant is named.

criterion: A limit of the method is reported and used to qualify findings
guiding_question: Does the paper report a limit of its own method and qualify its conclusions by that limit? NA allowed if the paper reports no executed method.
score_0_anchor: No method limit is reported and conclusions are unqualified.
score_1_anchor: A limit is reported, but at least one finding is not qualified by it.
score_2_anchor: A method limit is reported, and each finding is qualified by that limit.
